title: Jet-filtration weight estimates for singular points
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $X\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ a connected generically reduced closed subscheme of dimension one whose reduced support $D=X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is nondegenerate. Use the weighted flags and coefficients $a_F$ of [lem-sfb-bounded-hilbert-weight-polynomials]. Assume every reduced irreducible component of degree at most three is a rational normal curve. The following estimates hold.
(1) If $p\in D$ has multiplicity $t\ge3$ (the leading coefficient of $n\mapsto\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{D,p}/\mathfrak m_p^{n+1})$), the flag of forms vanishing at $p$, with weights zero there and one on its one-dimensional quotient, satisfies $\sum_iw_i=1$ and $a_F\ge t/2$.
(2) If the normalization of a reduced component $Y$ is ramified at a point $q$ above $p$ (its tangent map is zero there), then $\deg Y\ge4$. There is a weighted flag with $0\le w_i\le4$, $\sum_iw_i\le7$, and $a_F\ge8$. It is the jet flag giving weights $0,1,2,4$ to forms whose pullbacks to the normalized branch have orders at least $4$, at least $3$, at least $2$, and the remaining forms, respectively, with empty graded pieces omitted.
(3) Suppose every normalization map is unramified and every singular point of $D$ has multiplicity two. If such a point $p$ is not an ordinary node, there is a flag with weights in $\{0,1,2\}$, $\sum_iw_i\le3$, and $a_F\ge7/2$; when neither local branch belongs to a line component one has $a_F\ge4$. The flag assigns weight zero to forms vanishing on the common tangent line, weight one to the additional forms vanishing at $p$, and weight two to the remaining forms.
An ordinary node here means that the completed local ring is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The estimates are unchanged by a finite-length nilradical. No Hilbert semistability is assumed. A rational normal curve of degree $e$ means a smooth rational curve whose embedding in its own linear span is the complete degree-$e$ embedding of $\mathbf P^1$. Component degrees below are degrees of the pulled-back hyperplane line on the smooth normalized components [def-sc-normalization, def-pc-degree-line-bundle].

source.place: Section 3.2, Theorem 8 proof steps (4)--(6) and the cusp/tangent-line calculations, printed pp.14--15. Coefficients here are a_F=e_F/2, not e_F. The two tangent-line cases are also in Gieseker Proposition 1.0.6, printed pp.49--55. Local PDFs WANTED.

proof.text:
Work first on $D$ and write $L=\mathcal O_D(1)$. Finite type over the Noetherian field makes $D$ Noetherian and gives finitely many components. A zero-dimensional component would be a closed point disjoint from every other component (otherwise it is contained in one), hence an isolated open-and-closed point. Connectedness and dimension one exclude it, so $D$ is pure one-dimensional. For any chosen flag with maximum integral weight $B$, put $H_m=H^0(D,L^{\otimes m})$ and let $E_{m,j}$ be the span of restricted degree-$m$ monomials of weight at most $j$. For large $m$ the weight-polynomial node gives spanning and $w_F(m)=a_Fm^2+O(m)$. Sorting monomials by weight and retaining each vector that increases the span gives a basis whose number of weights greater than $j$ is exactly $\dim H_m-\dim E_{m,j}$. Any basis has at least that many. Thus
$$w_F(m)=\sum_{j=0}^{Bm-1}(\dim H_m-\dim E_{m,j}).$$
This is just the finite-dimensional greedy-basis argument, with each basis weight counted once for each smaller nonnegative integer.

proof.text:
For (1), let $V_p$ be the kernel of evaluation of ambient linear forms at $p$. Evaluation has rank one, so its zero/one flag has weight sum one. Every monomial of degree $m$ and weight at most $j<m$ has at least $m-j$ factors in $V_p$. At a normalized point $q$ above $p$ its order is therefore at least $b_q(m-j)$. The branch lemma gives $\sum_qb_q=t$ and $\sum_{q\in C_i}b_q\le e_i$, so these simultaneous jet orders have total at most $me_i$ on every component. The jet-codimension lemma gives $\operatorname{codim}E_{m,j}\ge t(m-j)-C$. Sum over $0\le j<m$ using step 1:
$$w_F(m)\ge t\,m(m+1)/2-Cm.$$
After division by $m^2$ and passage to the leading coefficient, $a_F\ge t/2$.

source.place: Section 3.2, Theorem 8 step (5), multiplicity flag; agent expansion; local PDF WANTED, read online.

proof.text: For (2), a component of degree at most three is a rational normal curve by hypothesis. On the degree-$e$ complete embedding of $\mathbf P^1$, on either standard affine chart ratios of consecutive monomial coordinates include the affine parameter, so the embedding and its normalization have nonzero tangent map. Thus the ramified component $Y$ has degree $e\ge4$. Trivialize $L$ near $p$ by an ambient linear form nonzero there and use a parameter $z$ on its normalized branch. Zero tangent map means every form vanishing at $p$ has order at least two, by the branch lemma. Successive conditions order at least $2,3,4$ have jumps of dimension at most one, since each records one coefficient of $k[[z]]$; evaluation at $p$ has rank one. Therefore the displayed jet flag has one weight-$4$ quotient, at most one weight-$2$ quotient, at most one weight-$1$ quotient, and weight sum at most seven. For every basis vector, its order plus its weight is at least four, including vectors that vanish identically on $Y$.

source.place: Section 3.2, Theorem 8 step (4), cusp flag and higher ramification; agent expansion; local PDF WANTED, read online.

proof.text:
A degree-$m$ monomial of weight at most $j<4m$ in the flag of step 3 has order at least $4m-j$ at the chosen normalized point. Since $e\ge4$, the jet-codimension lemma applies to this single point for every such $j$ and gives $\operatorname{codim}E_{m,j}\ge4m-j-C$. Hence step 1 yields
$$w_F(m)\ge\sum_{j=0}^{4m-1}(4m-j-C)=8m^2+O(m).$$
It follows that $a_F\ge8$. Missing jet graded pieces only decrease the sum of weights, and the argument does not require an ordinary cusp or characteristic zero.

source.place: Section 3.2, cusp Riemann--Roch calculation, printed pp.14--15; agent expansion; local PDF WANTED, read online.

proof.text:
For (3), at a nonnodal point of multiplicity two the branch lemma, applied to the nonzero tangent maps, gives exactly two normalized points and a common projective tangent line $T$. Forms vanishing on $T$ have order at least two at both points. The inclusions of the codimension-two space $V_T$ in the codimension-one space $V_p$ and then in $k^r$ give the specified weights $0,1,2$, with sum $1+2=3$. If neither branch is on a line component, the two component degrees are at least two when they are distinct. If the two points belong to one normalized component, that component has degree at least four: a degree-at-most-three rational normal component has only one preimage of each point. Thus on each component the simultaneous orders $2m-j$ at the selected points sum to at most its degree times $m$. Every weight-at-most-$j$ monomial has at least these orders. The jet-codimension lemma and step 1 give
$$w_F(m)\ge\sum_{j=0}^{2m-1}(2(2m-j)-C)=4m^2+O(m),$$
so $a_F\ge4$.

source.place: Section 3.2, Theorem 8 step (6), tangent branches with neither on a line; agent expansion; local PDF WANTED, read online.

proof.text:
If a branch belongs to a line component, this component is $T$ itself. The other branch is on a different component of degree at least two: two distinct projective lines through $p$ cannot have the same tangent line. On $T$ all weight-zero forms vanish identically, so any monomial nonzero on $T$ has weight at least $m$. For $0\le j<m$, $E_{m,j}$ therefore vanishes identically on $T$; impose only order $m$ at its preimage of $p$, and order $2m-j$ on the other branch. For $m\le j<2m$, impose order $2m-j$ on each branch. The totals respect the degree bounds on both components. The jet-codimension lemma gives respective codimension lower bounds $3m-j-C$ and $4m-2j-C$. Summing gives
$$w_F(m)\ge\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(3m-j-C)+\sum_{j=m}^{2m-1}(4m-2j-C)=\tfrac72m^2+O(m).$$
Thus $a_F\ge7/2$ also in this exceptional tangent-line case.

source.place: Section 3.2, tangent-line exception after the cusp calculation, printed p.15; agent expansion; local PDF WANTED, read online.

proof.text:
Finally compare $X$ and $D$ for any of these fixed flags. For large $m$ the ambient monomials span both section spaces, by the weight-polynomial node, and their restriction $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(m))\to H^0(D,L^m)$ is surjective. If the nilradical $N$ has finite length $\ell$, its twisted global sections have dimension at most $\ell$: the finite-support skyscraper lemma identifies them with the direct sum of the finitely many nonzero stalks, each twist is locally free of rank one, and a composition series at a closed $k$-point has one-dimensional factors. Left exactness of sections bounds the restriction kernel by $\ell$. From a minimum-weight monomial basis on $X$, select a subset mapping to a basis on $D$, which proves $w_{F,D}(m)\le w_{F,X}(m)$. Conversely lift a minimum-weight monomial basis on $D$ by the same monomials and extend it to a monomial basis on $X$. At most $\ell$ further monomials are needed, each of weight at most $Bm$. Therefore
$$0\le w_{F,X}(m)-w_{F,D}(m)\le B\ell m.$$
Their quadratic coefficients agree. This proves precisely the finite-length-nilradical invariance asserted, and transfers all three bounds to $X$, without any semistability assumption.
